At each fixed x, n+1 > ‖x‖ places x in the open ball where the cutoff is locally 1, so f_n and f agree near x and hence have the same genuine derivative at x. Mass is nonnegative and bounded by f². For entropy the zero-safe identity Φ(aq) = a Φ(q) + q Φ(a) gives |Φ(aq)| ≤ |Φ(q)| + q for 0 ≤ a ≤ 1 and q ≥ 0; a log a ≥ a−1, and a log a ≤ 0. Both terms in the envelope are integrable. At q = 1 and 0 < a < 1 the naive envelope |Φ(q)| fails.

Pointwise convergence and these envelopes give all three limits by dominated convergence on an arbitrary measure space. Compactness of closed bounded balls is only used in the later finite-dimensional compact-test extension, not the triple limit.

Point 1 checks the common scalar measurability and pointwise cutoff limit, plus the elementary L² mass domination. Point 3 checks the right mathematical obligations but prescribes the gradient product rule for the envelope, even though the prompt asks for an envelope rather than a method. Its alternative-argument clause modifies only pointwise convergence. For example, the cutoff is A/(n+1)-Lipschitz by the line-segment mean-value estimate. Together with local agreement this fully answers the prompt, but the literal criterion can withhold a whole point.
